questions.stem: At a multilingual workforce briefing, a supervisor proposes: "Rewrite the attendance roster so prior training appears current". The underlying case is: A department has repeated errors because a production target conflicts with the written safe procedure. Management requests refresher training. What should the safety professional do first? Which alternative is the most defensible correction?
options: Determine whether the performance gap is caused by knowledge, incentives, resources, supervision, or process design before prescribing training
Discipline all employees before examining the conflicting production system
Rewrite the attendance roster so prior training appears current
Deliver the same refresher course immediately because every performance problem is a training problem
questions.correctAnswerExplanation: Training is appropriate for a knowledge or skill gap, but it cannot by itself correct conflicting systems, incentives, equipment, or supervision. A performance analysis comes first.
incorrectOptionExplanations: The proposed response 'Discipline all employees before examining the conflicting production system' remains incomplete or misapplies the controlling training needs analysis principle.
The proposed response 'Rewrite the attendance roster so prior training appears current' remains incomplete or misapplies the controlling training needs analysis principle.

The proposed response 'Deliver the same refresher course immediately because every performance problem is a training problem' remains incomplete or misapplies the controlling training needs analysis principle.

questions.stem: At an adult-learning evaluation, a supervisor proposes: "Remove all hands-on practice so the course can finish earlier". The underlying case is: Experienced maintenance employees disengage from a lecture that repeats definitions they already know. Which redesign best uses adult-learning principles? Remove all hands-on practice so the course can finish earlier
